title: Rainwater harvesting for the Kadıköy block
description: A sketch of whether the apartment block should catch its own roof water: what we know, what we are guessing, who objected, and what we decided to try first.

nodes.name: The roof throws away every drop
nodes.description: 140 m² of bitumen roof sheds straight into the storm drain. If any of that is worth catching, everything else follows from it.

nodes.name: 810 mm a year, mostly November to March
nodes.description: Istanbul's long-run average. The supply is real but seasonal, so any store has to carry water from winter into summer or it is a winter-only toy.

metadata.sourceNote: Kandilli station 30-year mean, read off the published table

nodes.name: Two downpipes, both on the north face
nodes.description: The roof drains into exactly two pipes and both land in the north garden strip. Anything we install has to sit within a few metres of one of them.

nodes.name: How much non-potable water does the block actually use?
nodes.description: Garden, stairwell washing, the car park hose. Nobody has ever separated this from drinking water on the bill.

nodes.name: Shared meter reads 41 m³ a month
nodes.description: Across eight flats and the common areas. It is a ceiling, not an answer: it still mixes drinking water with everything else.

metadata.sourceNote: Twelve months of shared-meter invoices in the building folder

nodes.name: The shared fund holds about 60,000 TRY
nodes.description: And the facade repair already has a claim on part of it. Whatever we do first has to leave that repair funded.

nodes.name: Buried 5 m³ cistern in the north strip
nodes.description: The version that would actually carry winter water into July. Also the version that involves an excavator and a permit conversation.

nodes.name: Two 1 m³ tanks on the service balcony
nodes.description: Small, reversible, no digging. Covers the garden through spring and nothing more, but it can be installed in an afternoon.

nodes.name: Do nothing until the facade work is done
nodes.description: The honest baseline. Set aside once we realised the drum trial costs almost nothing and answers the demand question either way.

nodes.name: A buried tank may count as a structural change
nodes.description: Hülya thinks the municipality would want drawings for anything excavated. Unconfirmed, and it would delay the cistern by a season if true.

nodes.name: Standing water breeds mosquitoes in August
nodes.description: Applies to both storage options. Solvable with sealed lids and a first-flush diverter, but it is the objection the neighbours will raise first.

nodes.name: What bursts when the balcony tanks freeze?
nodes.description: Mert's objection, and it is a good one: the service balcony is unheated and the January minimum here has gone below -5 °C twice in the last decade.

nodes.name: Tape a rain gauge to the parapet for one winter
nodes.description: Cheap way to find out whether the station average holds over our own roof, or whether the neighbouring block's height shelters us.

nodes.name: Run one downpipe into a 200 L drum for a month
nodes.description: Measures both sides at once: how fast the roof fills a container, and how fast the garden empties it.

nodes.name: Hülya, building manager
nodes.description: Holds the shared fund and every past correspondence with the municipality. Nothing gets installed without her agreement.

nodes.name: Mert, the plumber who did the risers
nodes.description: Knows where every pipe in the building runs, and is the only person here who has seen a frozen balcony line.

nodes.name: Start with the balcony tanks
nodes.description: Cheap, reversible, and it buys a season of real numbers. Insulate the run and fit a drain valve for January.

nodes.name: Revisit the cistern when the scaffolding is up
nodes.description: The excavator and the facade crew want the same strip of garden. Doing them together is the only version anyone will approve.
